claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The as-cast alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
A post-solidification heat treatment can induce controlled in situ precipitation of fine L12-type nanoprecipitates in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The heat treatment will produce a uniform distribution of coherent nanoscale precipitates within the matrix.
Fine L12 precipitates can enhance alloy strength.
The nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion through dislocation bowing and bypass behavior.
The nanoprecipitates will inhibit crack nucleation and propagation in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Coherency of the nanoprecipitates will minimize interference with the reversible structural phase transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The heat-treated alloy will have significantly greater compressive strength than the as-cast alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will show reduced cracking relative to the as-cast alloy.
The heat-treated alloy's caloric response will remain essentially unchanged, with no more than a 10% decrease relative to the as-cast control.
The mechanical and caloric benefits will persist during cycling under applied magnetic fields, pressure fields, relevant temperatures, and mechanical loading.
The intervention maintains a rare-earth-free alloy composition.
